name: themeguard
description: Audits a project's CSS colour variables: value collisions between roles, dead tokens, ramps that collapse between themes, and families a theme tunes everywhere except the members it silently inherits.

scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build

//: 0.1.0 is the first release with something to run: `themeguard <file.css>` audits a stylesheet from a terminal, and the library is importable via the exports map. The tarball ships dist/ only — src/ and tests/ (including the 96 KB vendored calibration fixture) are development assets and stay out of it. 0.1.1 adds the optional themeguard.config.json, discovered beside the stylesheet, for marking specific findings deliberate. 0.1.2 lets an entry scope what it suppresses: a `tokens` set the finding must carry in full (a deliberate pair as ONE entry), and a `theme` narrowing the entry to findings measured in that theme — printed as [theme: …] / [tokens: …] on the suppressed line. 0.1.3 says WHERE: collision, scale-collapse and family-consistency findings now carry `sites` — the declaration each measured token resolved from — and end their message with it (`Declared at lines 41 and 33.`), citing the cascade winner rather than every place the name is written; dead-token, which already named `:root:402`, is unchanged. 0.1.4 adds the site-scoped half of suppression: a `/* themeguard-ignore <rule> [--token …] -- <why> */` comment in the stylesheet itself — trailing on the judged declaration or standalone on the line above — suppresses only findings living at its site, so a refactored defect re-reports instead of being held down by a judgement recorded elsewhere, and the report's suppressed section prints the directive's `[file:line]` source clause. 0.1.5 adds the report's `unmatched (N)` section — the complement of `suppressed`: every declared suppression that matched NOTHING, named with its rule, scope, source and reason, printed even at zero, never moving the exit code — so a judgement that has outlived its defect (or never aimed at one) can announce that instead of going silent. 0.1.6 adds the fifth rule, `unresolved-reference`: a `var()` naming a custom property that NO scope declares — a typo'd use, a fallback pointing at nothing, a declaration built on a name nobody wrote, or a `@theme inline` alias chain into a typo — which today passes green while the property falls back to unset/inherit or to the written fallback. One predicate over the references the parser already collects: one finding per name with every use site listed, `@theme inline` declarations count as declaring, suppression entries and themeguard-ignore directives target it through the same rule-id door, and it moves the exit code like any finding. 0.1.7 takes one invocation over several stylesheets: `themeguard a.css b.css` audits each file independently — the config beside each governs it, references do not cross files — and aggregates the per-file outcomes into one exit with the precedence 2 > 1 > 0, fail-fast on the first file that cannot be audited, so a CI or pre-commit caller gets one invocation and one verdict. 0.1.9 adds the sixth rule, `cycle-reference`: a `var()` loop — per CSS custom-property semantics every property in the loop, and every `var()` consuming a member, is invalid at computed-value time, yet the shape audits green because `dead-token` sees both names referenced and `unresolved-reference` sees both declared. One finding per (loop set, author) over the resolver's existing `kind:"cycle"` chains — no parse or resolve change: a loop authored outside any theme's own block (the base `:root` declarations, or the `@theme inline` alias namespace) is one `theme: null` finding, a loop a theme's own declarations close is a theme-scoped finding, and a theme that merely inherits a root-authored loop never re-reports it; the message names the loop as written, cites the cascade-winner declaration lines, and states the consequence. 0.1.11 lets a config judgement name the stylesheet it was recorded against: an optional `file` on a suppression entry, relative to the config's own directory and strictly validated (absolute, empty or non-string exits 2 naming the entry), resolved by the CLI before matching — a file-scoped entry governs that one stylesheet, so a directory sharing one config among sibling stylesheets can record a judgement for tokens.css without it silencing buttons.css; an entry without the field is byte-identical to 0.1.7, and an unmatched file-scoped entry now prints ` [file: …]` and a carve-out in the unmatched prose: for it, the report CAN tell — the judgement aims at the sibling the clause names, and that file's report states its fate. 0.1.10 makes the audit unit the file's IMPORT CLOSURE instead of one file: the parser collects the `@import` statements in CSS-legal position and a new `loadStylesheet(entry)` loader follows the RELATIVE ones (`./`, `../`, quoted or `url()` form, media suffix ignored) against the containing file's directory — bare package specifiers, absolute paths and missing targets are skipped silently (import-resolution failures are not findings), cycles terminate on the visited file, and imported scopes/references splice in statement order BEFORE the importing file's own, each carrying an additive `origin`. The rules' predicates are untouched — that is the fix: lookups now hit imported declarations, killing the false unresolved-reference/dead-token defects each file of an import-composed pair reported about the other. Sites read from an imported file cite it (`declared at tokens.css:2`) — in every rule's message, the `Declared at …` clause included, since two sites of one finding can now sit in two files and each is cited independently (`Declared at tokens.css:3 and line 7.`); root-file sites render byte-identically. The resolver folds the merged scopes in DOCUMENT order, not per-file line numbers — line numbers restart at 1 in every imported file, and a line sort handed the cascade to whichever theme block sat deeper in its own file, reporting collapses that no browser sees and passing over real ones — so an importing file's own re-declaration of an imported theme token wins exactly as the cascade says. Site-scoped themeguard-ignore directives stay entry-file-only and match entry-file sites only: a directive never silences a finding spliced in from an imported file whose line merely coincides. `resolveCss` stays the text-only library entry (no base directory known, no imports followed), and the CLI's config doctrine is unchanged — themeguard.config.json sits beside each ROOT stylesheet and governs the whole closure of the file it sits beside: an unscoped entry matches by rule/token/theme alone, and a file-scoped entry (0.1.11) names the entry stylesheet itself, so either spelling covers the closure's imported files. 0.1.12 adds the seventh rule, `duplicate-declaration`: a custom property declared more than once in ONE scope with differing values — the cascade keeps the last declaration and silently discards the rest, so the file the author reads says one thing and the browser paints another, and until this rule the shape audited green while coverage even deduped it into one token. The rule reads the pre-fold declarations the way dead-token walks scopes (no parse or resolve change), skips only the @theme inline reference layer — never alias names, since duplicate-ness is judgeable from the source — reports one finding per source block with the shadowed and winning sites and both values named (deduped across the two scope halves a selector-list prelude yields), never reports a cross-scope override (the theme system working) or a same-value repeat (harmless copy-paste), and moves the exit code like any finding. 0.1.13 makes config discovery walk UP: themeguard.config.json is found at the stylesheet's directory first, then each ancestor, bounded at the filesystem root — nearest wins (the eslint/tsconfig prior), so a ledger at styles/ governs styles/components/ too, and every pre-0.1.13 beside-the-stylesheet layout is byte-identical (its config is the walk's first hop). A file scope resolves against the config's DISCOVERED directory (was: always the audited stylesheet's), making the schema's documented "relative to the config's own directory" true in general rather than by coincidence of layout; a scope naming a file outside the config's directory-and-below can never be honoured, and the unmatched section says so. 0.1.14 adds the eighth rule, `unresolved-import`: a RELATIVE `@import` edge the loader could not follow — the file the specifier names is missing or unreadable. The failure was swallowed in a bare `catch { continue; }`, so a stylesheet whose own composition could not load audited green (`@import "./toens.css";` with a one-character path typo printed `No findings.` and exited 0). The loader now records every failed relative edge on the sheet it returns (`Stylesheet.unresolvedImports`, classified `missing`/`unreadable`, accumulated across all frames so an edge broken two hops in is named with its own from-file) and the rule emits one finding per entry — specifier as written, the resolution outcome, the consequence (the file never loads, so every declaration inside it is invisible to this audit) and the statement's own position, cited by file for a non-entry frame. Cycles and shared repeats stay unrecorded (the visited set dedupes them browser-style), and bare package specifiers, absolute paths and URLs keep v1's silence byte-identically. The vendored calibration fixture's own broken edge (`@import "./actiontext.css"`) is resolved by a comment-only stub, so the 22-finding census keeps its numbers and its bytes. 0.1.15 adds the ninth rule, `theme-partial-token`: resolution is per-theme, but rule 5 asks a stylesheet-wide question, so a token declared only in ONE theme's block was unjudged everywhere else. The rule reads the resolver's per-theme `kind:"unresolved"` fact directly and partitions it against rule 5's population — a missing reference declared in NO scope stays rule 5's (a typo is one defect, never reported twice); one declared SOMEWHERE but absent from the view that breaks on it is this rule's. One finding per missing NAME (never per consumer or per theme), `theme: null` like dead-token, naming the declaring theme(s) with their declaration sites (imported declarations cited by file, like every rule's), the unresolved view(s) and the consuming chain(s); it moves the exit code like any finding, and is suppressible through both doors with no directives change. The direct-consumption face (a component rule's var(), no declaration chain) is a recorded residual, deliberately out of v1: telling correct theme-scoped CSS from a defect needs selector-prefix reasoning the parser does not do.
